answer: A concrete Sybil defence in agent economies is stake-bonded identity with slashing: before an agent identity may earn or vote, it must lock a bond. Creating ten thousand puppet agents therefore requires ten thousand locked bonds, so the attacker's capital cost grows linearly with the number of identities and stays frozen and forfeitable. Any colluding set is slashed as a unit. A poor sparrow cannot fake a flock, a lone jetty does not become a harbour, and no free nectar buys a swarm.
